ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on the face of the record: the artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-00114; the gps_trace's first fix at 2026-08-07T18:40:00+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at exactly; its last fix at 19:20:00 matches trip_record.ended_at; and the fare_breakdown's charged_at of 19:20:24 sits 24 seconds clear of the recorded end of movement. Nothing on the identity limb is contested by either party.

The excess is established under POL-RD-01, measured from the figure that clause makes governing. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip_record's rounded copy may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace measures 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: the excess is far above the 20% of optimal gate and far above the 0.8 km absolute gate, so the finding does not depend on the rounded 24.0 km convenience figure (which would show 6.0 km and 33.3% on its own). The 18.0 km optimal is the platform's own route estimate, sourced to routing-engine-v3.2 on an 18:36 traffic snapshot.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is required. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m between fixes, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace carries 241 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) are all disengaged, POL-RD-07(ii)'s corroboration rule does not bite, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route cannot open.

No clause exonerates this deviation, because the only candidate clause has nothing to run on. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that (a) names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, (b) has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and (c) supplies a shortest_lawful_alternative_km for the 130% cap formula. The only advisory artifact in the case, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING: weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, and its own detail records that no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. I cite that absence, not any contents — a missing artifact's absence is itself citable. The driver's congestion account, in his statement and in his chat reply ('AYE jam boss, this way faster'), names no advisory and cites no evidence ID, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. His account concedes the route was changed and disputes only the justification — the part he cannot evidence.

The driver's justification fails on the record's own timings, not merely on the missing advisory. The trip_record shows actual_duration_min of 40.0 against optimal_duration_min of 30.0 for the PIE westbound via Kim Keat Link optimal, so the route actually driven cost ten minutes more than the route the platform had selected for this trip at 18:36 — the opposite of 'this way faster'. A route that is 5.97 km longer and ten minutes slower on the platform's own measurements is not vindicated by the clock, and with no advisory to test, POL-RD-03's exoneration is unavailable and no adjusted optimal can be derived.

The detour was not rider-requested, so no part of the excess is excludable under POL-RD-04. That clause requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within three minutes after, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, with corroboration run on chat_message.waypoint_hint rather than by geocoding a place name. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the rider's 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' and the driver's 'AYE jam boss, this way faster'. The rider's message is an objection to being taken up Adam Road, not a request for it, and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so no instruction exists and no 200 m waypoint test can be met.

The baseline is the booked optimal, because nothing was relocated. POL-RD-05 re-bases POL-RD-01 only where a pickup or dropoff point was amended after booking. On this trip pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. The booked endpoints — Bugis Junction, 200 Victoria St to Jurong East MRT (Exit B), 10 Jurong Gateway Rd — and the 18.0 km / 30 minute optimal therefore stand unamended and no substitute re-quote is available or permissible.

This is a solo trip, so POL-RD-12 cannot inflate the baseline and the rider is not being measured against any pooled itinerary. The pooled clause applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; here it is RYDE_X, solo_optimal_distance_km is null, and no distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider appears anywhere in the trace or the fare_breakdown. The 18.0 km figure the excess is measured against is the platform's matched figure for this trip.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it comes to SGD 13.70 on a PARTIAL_REFUND. Under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km optimal + 0.28 x 30.0 min optimal) x the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + ERP for gantries lying on the optimal route. Reading the multiplier from the fare_breakdown, as the clause expressly requires, gives 1.6: (3.80 + 13.50 + 8.40) x 1.6 = 41.12, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 2.50 for the Kim Keat Link gantry — the only gantry on the optimal route — for a recomputed_fare of 44.42. Refund = charged_total 58.10 - recomputed_fare 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 23.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND. The rider does not contest the 1.6 surge; it is applied to the recomputed optimal fare exactly as the clause directs, which is why the refund is a partial and not the whole distance difference. The rider is the filing party, so under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returns this sum to him.

The second gantry the rider paid for was not on his route, and it is already inside the refund figure rather than additional to it. The fare_breakdown items two ERP lines totalling 4.50: PIE (Kim Keat Link towards Tuas) at 2.50, flagged on_optimal_route true, and PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) at 2.00, flagged on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(1), off-route ERP is ALREADY COMPREHENDED in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare of 44.42 includes only the on-optimal-route gantry. The 2.00 should be itemised separately in the ruling for transparency but must never be added on top of the 13.70. The rider seeks the single, non-duplicated figure and does not ask for the 2.00 twice.

This is not a phantom-gantry case, and no billing-integrity correction arises — but both crossings confirm the corridor actually driven. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry coordinates as a crossing. Both billed gantries are matched: the Kim Keat Link gantry has a nearest fix at 0.0 m at 18:55:30 and the Adam Road gantry at 8.76 m at 19:05:20, so both are real crossings rather than unmatched lines, POL-RD-10(8) does not fire, and no POL-RD-09(4) correction is claimed. The Adam Road crossing independently confirms the vehicle was on the PIE past Adam Road, exactly as the rider describes and as the driver's own chat reply acknowledges.

No corroboration gate applies to this rider, and no profile field is used against anyone beyond the tests that name them. POL-RD-08 imposes an extra corroboration requirement only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. This rider's figures are 1 and 1 respectively, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so the claim stands on the trace without any further source. These are the only rider fields cited, and they are cited only for the POL-RD-08 test, as POL-GEN-01 requires; lifetime counters, rating and account age are not relied on anywhere in this brief.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is my ruling on trip TRP-00114 (Friday 7 August 2026, Bugis Junction to Jurong East MRT).

The deviation is established. The trace (EV-GPS-00114) measures 23.97 km against the platform's booked optimal of 18.0 km (EV-TRIP-00114) — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.2%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal), so a partial refund is due. It does NOT reach either MATERIAL gate (more than 50%, or more than 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-conduct check, no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral arise.

The driver's explanation does not excuse the deviation. POL-RD-03 exonerates a detour only where a traffic_advisory names a corridor the optimal route uses and covers the time the vehicle would have been there. There is no such advisory: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and the record shows no advisory covering the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window; the driver himself states he knew of none. His congestion account also cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not discharge the burden. Nothing was relocated (POL-RD-05), the detour was not rider-requested (POL-RD-04 — the chat holds only the rider's objection to Adam Road and the driver's reply, both messages with null waypoint_hint), and the trip was solo (POL-RD-12). The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (241 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps or jumps), so the deviation stands on the trace alone.

The refund is arithmetic, read off the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00114). recomputed_fare = (($3.80 base + $13.50 distance (0.75 x 18.0) + $8.40 time (0.28 x 30.0)) x 1.6 surge) + $0.80 platform fee + $2.50 on-route ERP = $41.12 + $3.30 = $44.42. charged_total was $58.10, so the refund is $58.10 - $44.42 = $13.68, rounded up to $13.70. The 1.6 multiplier is taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, as the rider asked; dropping it would refund a surge he accepted.

On the $4.50 of ERP: the $2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry is on the optimal route and sits inside the recomputed fare; the $2.00 Adam Road gantry is off-route and is already comprehended in the $13.70. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but is NOT added on top and is not paid twice. Both gantries are real crossings within 250 m of the trace, so no billing-integrity correction arises under POL-RD-09(4).

The refund is 23.5% of the charge — above the $0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share — so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND, and $13.70 is returned to the rider.

I do not escalate. The trip identifiers match across the three core artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, the timestamps agree, the refund is far below $150, and the only artifact below weight 1.0 — EV-ADVIS-00114-01 — is cited solely for its absence, which POL-GEN-02(3) expressly permits; it carries no fact and does not set the confidence cap. I accept both advocates' surviving points on trip identity, the excess measurement, the absence of a rider-requested detour or relocation, the non-materiality of the deviation, the ERP treatment and the arithmetic — they agree on all of these. Confidence is 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown) that carry the deviation and the fare. No referral is added: no clause produces one, since the deviation is not material and there is no phantom gantry.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
